DOGS

Dogs, it's something WFRP 3E eventually hit, but WFRP 4E hasn't quite managed yet.

But I'm going to go far further than ever before with this.

So, I'm writing about small but vicious dogs. And medium dogs. And large ones, too.

Why?

Well, the core book provides only a basic support for keeping and developing your own dogs (or any pets). We have a base statline for Dogs on page 315 and Wolves on page 317. We also have the rules for Henchmen on page 309.

Why are the Henchmen rules so important? Because they are specifically designed for, amongst other things, handling pets. Let's take a look at what they say?

In summary:

  • Pets are 'Henchmen'.
  • Henchmen have full Character Sheets and are given to a Player to play alongside their PC.
  • A Player's Henchmen earn half the XP of their PC.
  • This XP is spent as normal.

Sounds great. But, can you see the missing element here?

Yup, the Careers in Chapter 3 aren't exactly designed for dogs, or, indeed, any pets, so spending XP could prove a touch difficult.

So, I'm going to fix that.

However, before I do, there are more dog stats for us to look at. I added statlines for two breeds of dogs in Enemy in Shadows. These are the Telland Pit Bull on page 98, and the Ulzhammer Shepherd Dog on page 111. I also statted a 'Fighting Dog' to the Guide to Ubersreik, page 53, and there is the Dog used for pulling carts in the Enemy in Shadows Companion on page 22. No need to look 'em up if you don't have the books to hand; it's just good to note they exist for the moment, so you know everything I create below takes these into account.

So, looking at those, we have a Dog, a Draught Dog, a Wolf, a Pit Bull, Shepherd Dog, and a Fighting Dog all nicely statted and ready for careers. However, we don't have a single Small but Vicious Dog.

Call in the PCs, because this is a Warhammer crime that needs to be investigated!

It's time to do some doggo statting.

But, me being me, I'm not just going to do our Small But Vicious, I'm going to loosely cover all dogs. Coz it's my blog and I can.

To do that, I'm going to stat 8 different loose domesticated dog types that'll cover all the basics I'll need. The ones I'll go for are:

  • Herd Dogs
  • Hound Dogs
  • Hunting Dogs
  • Lap Dogs
  • Mongrel Dogs
  • Pit Dogs
  • Terrier Dogs
  • War Dogs


#AllTheDogs

Well, almost, I'm missing out some work doggos – you know, ones that pull sleds or the like, the aforementioned 'draught' dog from the Enemy in Shadows Companion – but I'll add these later. I already have enough for a small book here, as you'll soon see...

WFRP: Dogs

 

HORSES

The following WFRP Careers either begin with a horse or later require a horse (or mule) as Trappings for a higher Career level:

BEGIN

  • Cavalryman
  • Knight

LATER REQUIRE

  • Advisor
  • Bailiff
  • Bounty Hunter
  • Coachman
  • Entertainer
  • Herbalist
  • Hunter
  • Merchant
  • Messenger
  • Noble
  • Outlaw
  • Pedlar
  • Protagonist
  • Road Warden
  • Scout
  • Soldier
  • Villager
  • Warden
  • Warrior Priest
  • Watchman
  • Witch Hunter
  • Wizard

Wow... Stop the press. That's over a third of the Careers needing horsies. We need full rules for these, and stats! After all, we wouldn't want to leave our horsie friends without attributes, would we!

So, what do we need to resolve, horse-wise? Well, let's take a look through the Careers and see what riding animals are mentioned:

  • Destrier
  • Draught Horse
  • Light Warhorse
  • Horse (we can assume this means any horse you prefer)
  • Mule
  • Pony
  • Riding Horse

As expected, really, given these are all the horsies mentioned in the Consumer Guide in WFRP on page 306. It's almost like I planned it that way...

But are all these equids properly statted in the rulebook?

There are stats for the following riding animals (assuming we discount 'monsters' like Pegasi or Demigryphs and so on) in WFRP's bestiary in Chapter 12:

  • @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-core.actors.Actor.b1R5sW6lYIViJ2ki]{Horse}

Are there any other rules to reference?

Thankfully, yes. There is much more horsey goodness to be found on pages 22–24 in the Enemy in Shadows Companion; we also get stats for:

  • Draught Horse
  • Heavy Warhorse (Destrier)
  • Light Warhorse (Hobby)
  • Pony/Donkey/Mule
  • Riding Horse (Palfrey)
  • Heavy Draught Horse

That's much better. But I also have two primary issues.

1) Ponies, Donkies, and Mules are all given the same stats, but are quite different animals in real life.
2) Ponies also cost double the price of Mules and Donkeys, but have the same stats.

WHRP: Horses

 

CATS

WFRP4 needs a Cat. It has no cats*. And that's cattist. This, for example, opens the Cat up to the Beast Form Spell (WFRP, page 245) and if you happen to be a Ranaldan with the Cat's Eyes Miracle, you have some actual stats to reference, too.

*: Well, beyond the 'Great Cat{Great Cats}', found in the Enemy in Shadows Companion, but they are far from normal cats.

WHFP: Cats
